Bug_Details: Calling Iterator.hasNext() is not supposed to have any side effects and hence should not change the iterator’s state. Iterator.next() advances the iterator by one item. So calling it inside Iterator.hasNext() breaks the hasNext() contract and will lead to unexpected behavior in production.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by calling iterator.next() inside the iterator.hasNext() loop condition. This violates the contract of hasNext() which should not change the state of the iterator.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered because the method'showBug' incorrectly calls 'iterator.next()' inside the 'while (iterator.hasNext())' loop, which violates the contract of 'hasNext()' not having side effects.
